Why “Backbone,” “Embedding,” and “Prior” Feel Like a Foreign Language Even After Years in the Field

10 min read
Just now

--

Disclosure: I use GPT search to collection facts. The entire article is drafted by me.
Here’s the actual problem, stated precisely: most people studying computer vision don’t lack vocabulary. They lack a map that shows where each term sits relative to the others. You can memorize twenty definitions and still feel lost reading a paper, because the definitions were never the point — the relationships were.
This piece builds that map. Not a glossary. A blueprint of how information moves through a vision system, and why each term exists as a checkpoint along that path.
The core claim, upfront
Almost every CV term you’ve struggled with — Backbone, Head, Neck, Embedding, Feature Map, Pooling, Prior, Semantic, Fine-tuning — is not a mathematical concept. It’s an engineering label, invented by researchers who needed a shorthand for a specific stage in an information-compression pipeline. Once you see the pipeline, the vocabulary stops being a memorization problem and becomes a description of mechanics you already understand.
